content_units: For   2 adults  , a   180,000 JPY   ground budget over   2026-04-12 to 2026-04-16   is realistic for a calm, culture-focused Kyoto trip if you stay in a mid-range hotel and use mostly trains/buses plus walking. This plan prioritizes   temples, gardens, tea culture, and quiet neighborhoods  , with relaxed pacing and a   shellfish-aware food approach  .
Hotel (4 nights)   88,000   Mid-range machiya-style stay or quiet business hotel,  22,000/night
Local transport   12,000   IC card use, buses/subway/JR for 2 adults
Temple/garden admissions   18,000   Covers the listed highlights
Small shopping/contingency   12,000   Snacks, extra taxi, souvenirs
Day 1: Higashiyama South and Gion Edge
-   Morning:   Start at   Kiyomizu-dera   early to avoid crowds, then walk downhill through   Sannenzaka   and   Ninenzaka   at a slow pace.
-   Afternoon:   Visit   Kodai-ji   and its garden, then continue into the quieter side streets near   Ishibei-koji  .
-   Dinner:   Choose a tofu or obanzai restaurant around Gion/Higashiyama; ask for   no shellfish, no fish stock if needed  .
-   Rainy-day backup:   Replace the slope-heavy walk with   Kyoto National Museum   plus a long tea break nearby.
- Take a bus or taxi to Kiyomizu area   before 8:00 AM   to avoid congestion.
- Walk downhill rather than uphill to keep the day easy.
- In Gion/Higashiyama, walking is often faster than short bus hops.
Day 2: Arashiyama Bamboo, Garden Calm, and River Views
-   Morning:   Arrive early in   Arashiyama   for the   Bamboo Grove  , then visit   Tenryu-ji   and its garden.
-   Afternoon:   Cross   Togetsukyo Bridge   and spend a quiet stretch around the river; if energy allows, visit   Okochi Sanso Garden  .
-   Dinner:   Riverside soba, yudofu, or grilled chicken set meal; confirm broth ingredients.
-   Rainy-day backup:   Spend more time at   Tenryu-ji  , then visit   Saga Arashiyama Museum of Arts & Culture   or a long lunch/tea session.
- Use the   JR Sagano Line   from Kyoto Station for a simple start.
- Arashiyama gets crowded by late morning, so this is best as an early day.
- Consider a taxi back if tired; it can be worth it after a long walking day.
Day 3: Uji Tea Day and Byodo-in
-   Morning:   Take the train to   Uji  . Visit   Byodo-in Temple   first, then walk the riverside slowly.
Morning:   Take the train to   Uji  . Visit   Byodo-in Temple   first, then walk the riverside slowly, Kyoto, Japan
-   Afternoon:   Enjoy a   tea tasting or matcha sweets stop  , browse tea shops, and visit   Taihoan Tea House   if open during your dates.
-   Dinner:   Return to Kyoto for a quiet dinner near your hotel, or eat in Uji before heading back.
-   Rainy-day backup:   Keep the Uji plan but focus on   Byodo-in Museum  , covered tea shops, and an indoor tea experience.
- Use   JR Nara Line   from Kyoto Station for convenience.
- Uji is ideal as a lower-stimulation day with fewer major transfers.
- Buy tea in small tins if luggage space is limited.
-   Morning:   Visit   Ginkaku-ji   early, then walk part of the   Philosopher’s Path   at an easy pace.
-   Afternoon:   Continue to   Honen-in   or   Nanzen-ji   depending on energy; both suit a calm, reflective day.
-   Dinner:   Simple Kyoto-style set meal or vegetarian shojin-inspired dinner.
-   Rainy-day backup:   Focus on   Nanzen-ji subtemples   and a slow café/tea stop rather than the full outdoor walk.
- Use bus/subway combination, but avoid too many hops.
- The Philosopher’s Path is best done partially, not as a checklist march.
- If feet are tired, taxi between Ginkaku-ji and Nanzen-ji is a reasonable splurge.
Day 5: Daitoku-ji Area and Nishijin Calm
-   Morning:   Explore the   Daitoku-ji   temple complex and selected subtemples/gardens for one of Kyoto’s quieter cultural areas.
-   Afternoon:   Wander   Nishijin   or rest in a traditional café; if you want one final garden stop, add   Kyoto Botanical Gardens  .
-   Dinner:   Final Kyoto meal with tofu kaiseki, wagyu set, or vegetarian course that avoids shellfish.
-   Rainy-day backup:   Spend longer at temple interiors/subtemples, then do a tea house or craft-focused afternoon.
- This area is calmer than central sightseeing districts and works well for your final day.
- Keep this day flexible in case you want to revisit a favorite temple or café.
- If departure is later that night, store luggage at hotel or station rather than carrying it around.
Food and Transport Notes for a Relaxed Trip
- In Japan, shellfish may appear in mixed seafood dishes, broths, or sauces.
-   Kaihsen, eb, kani, kai wa taberaremasen   (I cannot eat seafood/shrimp/crab/shellfish)
-   Dashi ni mo hairanai hou ga ii desu   (Better if it is not in the broth too)
- Chicken yakitori places with simple salt seasoning
- Use an   IC card   for buses, subway, and JR to keep transfers easy.
- Kyoto buses can be slow in sightseeing zones; use   JR/subway first  , then bus/taxi for the last stretch.
- For two adults, a   short taxi ride   can be worthwhile when moving between temple areas and saving energy.
This plan assumes   4 hotel nights   and a comfortable, mid-range stay in a quiet area such as   Higashiyama, Okazaki, or near Kyoto Shiyakusho-mae  , rather than nightlife-heavy districts.
